deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematical derivation, only qualitative natural philosophy in two parts.

(A) Conclusion of the molecular-forces passage from p. 31. Riemann sorts the forces acting between chemical atoms into two groups:
- Attractive: external pressure, and the capillary forces (cohesion and adhesion).
- Repulsive: thermal repulsion and chemical repulsion.
He then characterises each state of aggregation by which forces balance which:
- Gas: thermal repulsion alone balances external pressure.
- Liquid: thermal repulsion balances external pressure only with the help of chemical repulsion.
- Capillary forces alone, without external pressure, cannot balance the repulsive forces. They show up only in capillary phenomena.
The sentence on solids ("Bei dem festen ...") breaks off.

(B) An editorial note in double parentheses says the following text agrees in essence with Blatt 10/11 and is older than it. Then comes an early draft of Riemann's axioms of mechanics. He states that since Newton, besides the geometric axioms, the following hypotheses explain external perception:
- (1) Inertia: an isolated body stays at rest or moves uniformly in a straight line. In modern terms, with no force, d^2x/dt^2 = 0, so x(t) = x0 + v0*t.
- Riemann remarks that this law cannot be derived from the principle of sufficient reason. Persistence of motion must have a cause, and that cause can lie only in the inner state of matter.
- At every point of space, at every instant, there exists a cause determined in magnitude and direction. In modern terms this is a vector field F(x,t). Newton is said to have sought this cause in the motion of a stuff spread through infinite space (an aether); the editor adds '(?)'.

A second numbered list follows:
- (1) All changes of place are continuous, i.e. x(t) is continuous.
- (2) Every dead (inanimate) body, independently of any external force, continues in each moment the motion it had in the previous one (inertia restated).
- (3) At every point there is a cause determined in magnitude and direction which [changes] the motion of each body. The sentence is unfinished.

The next page develops this fully: forces compose by the parallelogram rule, and force/acceleration = mass. That is Newton's second law, F = m a, in Machian-style operational form.

No computations occur. The fragment serves Riemann's programme of reducing gravitation and other forces to the state of a space-filling medium.
errors: The machine transcription's 'die chemische Repulsion nur mit Hülfe der chemischen' is self-contradictory. The manuscript reads 'die thermische Repulsion nur mit Hülfe der chemischen', which also matches the scheme set out on p. 31.
No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics. Several statements are left unfinished ('Bei dem festen', 'Ursache . . .', 'welche der Bewegung jedes physischen Körpers . . .').

results.what: Classification of states of aggregation by the balance of attractive forces (pressure, capillary) against repulsive forces (thermal, chemical).
results.modern_name: Qualitative molecular-force theory of gas/liquid/solid states (precursor of kinetic/van der Waals picture)
results.usually_credited_to: General 19th-century physics (Laplace, Poisson capillarity; later van der Waals 1873)

results.what: Newton's first law, with the claim that persistence of motion needs a cause located in the inner state of matter.
results.modern_name: Law of inertia; Riemann's medium-based (aether) philosophy of force
results.usually_credited_to: Newton 1687 (law); Riemann's Naturphilosophie fragments (published in Werke 1876, ed. Weber/Dedekind)

results.what: Postulate of a field: a cause determined in magnitude and direction at every point and every instant, possibly rooted in the motion of a space-filling stuff.
results.modern_name: Vector force field / field-theoretic (aether) conception of gravitation
results.usually_credited_to: Faraday/Maxwell (field concept); Riemann's 'Gravitation und Licht' fragments

deep.surprise_reason: This is qualitative natural philosophy that closely parallels Riemann's published Nachlass fragments on Naturphilosophie (Werke, 'Gravitation und Licht' / Newtonian hypotheses). The editorial note itself says it duplicates Blatt 10/11. Nothing in it is new or mathematical.

checkable.asserts: With no force (zero acceleration), motion is uniform and rectilinear, x = C1 + C2*t. This is hypothesis 1, the law of inertia.
Force divided by change of motion gives a constant quotient, the mass. This is the next page's definition, consistent with F = m*a.

transcription_corrections: Line 1-2: 'ist die chemische Re-pulsion nur mit Hülfe der chemischen' should read 'ist die thermische Re-pulsion nur mit Hülfe der chemischen'.
Pencil margin note near the crossed-out mark is unclear; it looks like 'bis zu 7.' / 'Stück 7.' and is uncertain.
Faint pencil 'Naturgesetz' in the middle margin is plausible but very faint; it could also be 'Naturphil.'.
